rows.title: Inflation unchanged at 3.1% in October: StatCan
rows.summary: Statistics Canada said on Monday that Canada's annual inflation rate held at 3.1% in October, the same as in September, keeping it just above the Bank of Canada's 1–3% target range. Gasoline was the biggest driver: pump prices were 30.9% higher than a year earlier, up from 27.8%, even though they fell 2.5% from September. StatCan said part of the jump is a base effect, because crude oil prices were low in October 2025, and it pointed to ongoing conflict in the Middle East and Ukraine. Excluding energy, inflation edged down to 2.0% from 2.1%, while grocery prices picked up to 2% after four months of slowing and rent growth eased. The release matters for interest rates, since the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.5% on October 28 and is watching whether high energy costs spread to other prices.
rows.fact: StatCan's October CPI shows annual inflation steady at 3.1%, with gasoline up 30.9% year over year and inflation excluding energy easing to 2.0%. The agency described price pressure as broad-based, led by gasoline, natural gas, groceries and clothing, while rent growth slowed and cellphone plan prices fell.
rows.why: 휘발유 같은 한 품목이 전체 물가 상승률을 얼마나 끌어올릴 수 있는지, 그리고 중앙은행이 금리를 정할 때 왜 '에너지를 뺀 물가'를 따로 보는지 배울 수 있는 좋은 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a single item like gasoline can push up the overall inflation rate, and why central banks look separately at inflation excluding energy when setting interest rates.
rows.term_def: A year-over-year change that looks big or small mainly because of what happened in the same month last year. If gas was unusually cheap last October, this October's price looks like a huge jump even if prices didn't rise much recently.
rows.note: StatCan October 2026 CPI, released Nov 16 at 8:30 a.m. ET. CP figures cross-checked against Reuters' report (3.1% y/y, 0.2% m/m, ex-energy 2.0%, CPI-median 2.0%, CPI-trim 1.8%, gasoline +30.9%), Global News and BNN Bloomberg. The Oct 28 BoC hike to 2.5% is from CP's Nov 13 preview.

opinion.title: Canada CPI Holds at 3.1%, but Softer Core Inflation Challenges Further BoC Tightening
opinion.author: ActionForex (staff)
opinion.summary: This commentary notes that October inflation came in at 3.1%, below the 3.2% forecast, and monthly prices rose 0.2% against an expected 0.3%. It argues that headline inflation is high mainly because of energy, while underlying inflation is fairly restrained: CPI-median held at 2.0%, CPI-trim eased to 1.8%, and inflation excluding energy slipped to 2.0%, all close to the 2% target. Its conclusion is that the report gives the Bank of Canada less reason to raise rates again in December than a hotter reading would have. It adds two caveats: CPI-common rose to 2.5%, and groceries and clothing are heating up again. So the Bank may simply move more cautiously rather than declare its rate hikes over.
opinion.why: 전체 물가와 '근원 물가'가 다르게 움직일 때 중앙은행이 금리 인상을 어떻게 판단하는지 보여 주어, 통화정책의 기본 논리를 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how a central bank weighs a rate hike when headline and core inflation send different signals, which helps explain the basic logic of monetary policy.

rows.title: Trump To Extend Shipping Waiver For Oil, Fertilizer For 90 Days
rows.summary: President Trump is extending his waiver of the Jones Act for another 90 days. The Jones Act normally requires cargo moving between US ports to travel on American-owned, American-flagged and American-crewed ships; the waiver lets companies use cheaper foreign-flagged vessels to move fuel, crude oil, LNG, soybean oil and fertilizer within the country. The new waiver starts on November 16 with no gap and restores the full scope of the original March order, which had been narrowed in August to case-by-case reviews. The White House is acting because of high energy prices caused by the war with Iran and cost-of-living worries after the midterm elections. About 90 million barrels of products have moved between US ports under the waiver since March, with California getting the largest share, but shipbuilders and their allies in Congress argue it undermines protections for domestic shipbuilding.
rows.fact: About 338 voyages have used foreign vessels under the waiver since March, according to government data analyzed by the Cato Institute. California received 23 million barrels of extra products, compared with 8 million in the same period a year earlier. It is the longest and broadest Jones Act waiver in more than 70 years; earlier presidents waived the law only for single voyages or short periods, such as after hurricanes.
rows.outlook: Oil and chemical companies credit the waiver with offsetting supply disruptions from the Iran war, while shipbuilders warn it weakens rules they consider vital to US shipbuilding.
rows.why: 보호무역 규제를 잠시 풀었을 때 국내 운송비와 연료 공급이 어떻게 달라지는지 보여 주어, 무역 장벽이 소비자와 산업에 주는 비용과 편익을 실제 사례로 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows what happens to domestic shipping costs and fuel supply when a protectionist rule is temporarily lifted, a real-world lesson in the costs and benefits of trade barriers.
rows.term_def: Government policies that shield domestic industries from foreign competition, for example by requiring American-built ships. They can protect local jobs, but they often raise costs for consumers.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (White House decision reported Fri Nov 13 ET; waiver takes effect Nov 16; no US federal policy action or headline data with readable coverage in the last 24h). Full Bloomberg text read via gCaptain republication; cross-checked against the Washington Examiner (Nov 13).

opinion.title: A Case for Giving the Jones Act a Two-Year Time Out
opinion.author: James Carter (former deputy assistant secretary for economic policy, US Treasury)
opinion.summary: Written just before the November 15 expiry, the column asks the President and Congress to suspend the Jones Act for two years rather than keep renewing it with 60- and 90-day waivers. Carter argues that short waivers create uncertainty, making companies reluctant to sign multiyear contracts, charter ships or build facilities. Citing a Cato Institute analysis, he says foreign-flagged vessels made more than 300 voyages carrying over 80 million barrels since March, including record deliveries to the West Coast, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico, while no Jones Act tanker was idled. He cites estimates that the law costs Puerto Rico about $1.4 billion a year, roughly like a 30.6 percent tariff on mainland goods. He also argues national-security goals are better served by programs such as the Maritime Security Program, and that a two-year trial would let policymakers measure the real effects on costs, capacity and jobs.
opinion.why: 규제의 '불확실성'이 기업의 투자 결정을 어떻게 막는지, 그리고 운송 규제가 사실상 관세처럼 작동한다는 경제 원리를 쉽게 이해할 수 있기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains how policy uncertainty discourages business investment, and how a shipping rule can work like a hidden tariff.

rows.title: Lee calls for easier, more frequent M&As to normalize market
rows.summary: At a capital-market policy meeting at the Korea Exchange on Nov. 13, President Lee Jae Myung said mergers and acquisitions, including hostile takeovers, should become easier and more common. He argued that the threat of outside buyers would push controlling shareholders to improve corporate governance and help fix the long-running undervaluation of Korean stocks. Lee also called for an overhaul of the tech-focused Kosdaq market, covering listing, delisting and valuation, and for strict enforcement of delisting rules so weak firms leave the market quickly. The meeting followed a steep slide: the KOSPI fell from a record above 9,000 in June to the 5,000 range, and the Kosdaq dropped from its April record of 1,226 to around 700. The Korea Exchange said English-language disclosure will be extended to Kosdaq firms and it is considering requiring listed companies to hold at least one investor-relations event a year.
rows.fact: Lee called hostile M&A the key mechanism for normalizing the market and asked whether some controlling shareholders keep share prices low to cut inheritance taxes. He proposed a high-level task force of officials, ruling and opposition lawmakers, exchanges and investment associations to coordinate the reforms. The government has already tightened delisting rules, including higher minimum market-cap requirements and stricter criteria for stocks priced under 1,000 won.
rows.outlook: In a Nov. 16 follow-up, analysts including SK Securities' Na Seung-doo said the meeting offered little detail on attracting big institutional investors to the Kosdaq and called for a quick launch of the Kosdaq Select Index and ETFs tracking it.
rows.why: 주가가 왜 '저평가'되는지, 그리고 적대적 인수합병과 상장폐지 같은 제도가 기업 지배구조와 투자자 신뢰를 어떻게 바꾸는지 실제 정책 사례로 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It is a real policy case that shows why stocks can be 'undervalued' and how rules on hostile takeovers and delisting can change corporate governance and investor trust.
rows.term_def: An attempt by an outside buyer to gain control of a company without the agreement of its current management or controlling shareholders, usually by buying up a large share of its stock.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (policy meeting Nov 13 KST; no major government or BOK policy or data release in the last 24h — IMF Article IV results are due Nov 17). Full article bodies read; the column cites a slightly different KOSPI peak (June 19 intraday high of 9,385).

opinion.title: Stock market reform alone cannot stabilize share prices
opinion.author: Shin Sung-ho (former CEO of IBK Investment & Securities; member of the JoongAng Ilbo's Reset Korea Economic Committee)
opinion.summary: The guest columnist compares Korea's stock market this year with G7 markets, which rose steadily by about 11 percent with only small pullbacks, while the Kospi more than doubled to an intraday peak of 9,385 in June and then fell to 4,911 on Nov. 6. He argues that regulators and brokerages made investor losses worse through mishandled National Pension Service investments, risky leveraged single-stock ETFs, and hype that fed unrealistic expectations. He points to falling trust: brokerage customer deposits dropped from 139 trillion won in June to 92 trillion won by Nov. 12, as individuals moved money into foreign stocks. Writing after President Lee's Nov. 13 Korea Exchange meeting, he says regulatory fixes and government stock buying cannot hold prices up for long, citing past failures in Korea, Japan and China. He argues lasting stock values require broad structural reform of the economy, similar to Germany's Hartz labor reforms, rather than market-only measures.
opinion.why: 주가는 결국 경제의 실력을 반영한다는 원리, 즉 시장 제도 개선만으로는 한계가 있고 경제 구조 개혁이 필요하다는 시각을 정책 뉴스와 비교하며 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches the principle that stock prices ultimately reflect the strength of the real economy, so students can weigh market-rule reforms against the call for deeper structural reform.

rows.title: Eurozone posts €10.3 billion goods trade deficit in September
rows.summary: Eurostat's latest trade figures show the eurozone bought more goods from the rest of the world than it sold in September 2026, leaving a goods trade deficit of €10.3 billion. A year earlier the bloc had a €13.5 billion surplus, and markets had expected a smaller gap of about €4.5 billion. Imports grew far faster than exports (16.1% vs 6%), mostly because Europe is paying much more for imported oil and gas: the energy deficit widened from €20.7 billion to €33 billion. Europe's traditional strength in factory goods also faded, with the machinery and vehicles surplus shrinking from €10 billion to €3 billion. For the wider EU, exports to the US fell 10.6% and the trade deficit with China widened to €41.7 billion.
rows.fact: Euro area exports were €272.7 billion and imports €283.0 billion in September 2026. From January to September the eurozone ran a €36.5 billion deficit, compared with a €102.2 billion surplus in the same period of 2025. EU energy imports jumped 51.3% year on year to €51.5 billion.
rows.outlook: Eurostat publishes October trade figures on 16 December, and the European Commission releases its Autumn 2026 Economic Forecast on 17 November.
rows.why: 에너지를 수입에 의존하는 경제는 유가·가스 가격이 오르면 수출이 늘어도 무역수지가 적자로 바뀔 수 있다는 점, 즉 교역조건 악화가 국가 경제에 미치는 영향을 잘 보여주는 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how an energy-importing economy can swing into a trade deficit even while exports grow, because higher oil and gas prices worsen its terms of trade.
rows.term_def: The value of a country's goods exports minus its goods imports over a period; a positive number is a surplus and a negative number is a deficit.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (no major European government, ECB/BoE or Commission policy announcement or headline data release in the last 24h). Eurostat release of Nov 13; figures checked against the Eurostat release text reproduced by Hellenic Shipping News. Values are nominal, so price and volume effects are not separated.

opinion.title: Eurozone Trade Swings to Deficit as Energy Costs Rise and EU Manufacturing Surplus Shrinks
opinion.author: ActionForex (staff)
opinion.summary: This market note reads the September figures as evidence that the eurozone's trade position is weakening, not just having one bad month. It says the swing reflects a large gap between how fast purchases from abroad grew and how fast sales abroad grew, with costlier energy imports as the main driver. It argues the problem goes beyond energy, because Europe's traditional manufacturing surpluses in machinery, vehicles and chemicals also narrowed. It points to a shrinking EU surplus with the US and a wider deficit with China, and notes the year-to-date balance flipped from a large surplus into a deficit. Finally, it warns that nominal trade values alone cannot tell whether the change comes from higher prices or from changes in quantities traded.
opinion.why: 이 논평은 무역 통계를 읽을 때 '가격 효과'와 '물량 효과'를 구분해야 한다는 경제 분석의 기본 원칙과, 에너지 충격이 제조업 경쟁력 약화와 겹칠 때의 위험을 함께 생각해 보게 합니다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches the basic analytical habit of separating price effects from volume effects in trade data, and shows why an energy shock combined with weakening manufacturing competitiveness is a deeper concern.

rows.title: Japan's economy unexpectedly contracts as inflation squeezes households
rows.summary: Japan's Cabinet Office released its first estimate of July–September GDP on Monday: real output fell at an annualized 0.1%, the first decline in four quarters, while economists in a Reuters poll had expected 0.3% growth. Private consumption, more than half of the economy, fell 0.3% as persistent price increases, heavy rain and typhoons, and the fading of one-off purchases such as cars and air conditioners held spending back. Capital spending rose 1.6%, helped by labor-saving technology and AI projects. A jump in energy imports meant net external demand cut 0.6 percentage points from growth. Most analysts said the result probably won't stop the Bank of Japan, which raised rates in June and September, from hiking again as early as December, although continued weak consumption could split its board.
rows.fact: Measured quarter to quarter, GDP slipped only 0.02%, and the previous quarter was revised up to 1.7% annualized growth. Japan imports almost all its oil, and the war in Iran and a weak yen near 160 per dollar have pushed up energy costs.
rows.outlook: A Japan Center for Economic Research survey of 37 economists expects growth of about 0.9% in fiscal 2026 and about 1.0% in fiscal 2027, with the BOJ's December meeting the next key test.
rows.why: 수입 물가 상승이 가계의 실질 구매력을 깎아 소비를 위축시키면 GDP가 줄어들 수 있으며, 중앙은행은 경기 둔화와 물가 상승 사이에서 금리 결정을 고민해야 한다는 점을 보여 주는 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how rising import prices can eat into households' real purchasing power and shrink GDP, leaving a central bank to weigh a slowing economy against high inflation when it sets interest rates.
rows.term_def: A quarter's GDP change scaled up to show what the yearly rate would be if that pace lasted four quarters. Japan's 0.02% quarterly dip becomes about -0.1% annualized.
rows.note: Official Cabinet Office data released Nov 16 (JST). Reuters text via Daily Sabah, cross-checked against AP (Yuri Kageyama) and Seoul Economic Daily. China's October activity data came out the same day; Japan chosen for fuller readable coverage. C is a column published four days before the release, previewing the same Q3 GDP data.

opinion.title: Focus shifts from high prices to the consumption tax cut and the durability of the US AI boom (July–September GDP outlook) [translated from Japanese]
opinion.outlet: Nomura Research Institute (NRI), Global Economy & Policy Insight
opinion.author: Takahide Kiuchi, Executive Economist, Nomura Research Institute
opinion.summary: Kiuchi, a former Bank of Japan board member, previewed the Q3 GDP release and argued that consumption would be the weak spot because of oil-driven living costs, bad weather and the end of one-off demand for cars and air conditioners. He expected strong AI-related capital spending and exports to the US to offset part of that weakness, but rising imports to make net exports a drag, which is what the data later showed. He believes price increases may have peaked, since far fewer food price hikes were announced for November and December. He warns that the food consumption tax cut planned for April 2027 could be partly offset if firms raise prices in advance to avoid repricing twice. He concludes that in 2027 Japan's economy will depend more on whether the US AI investment boom lasts, because a downturn there could strengthen the yen and hurt exports, investment and wages.
opinion.why: 가격 전가, 메뉴 비용, 해외 수요가 수입·환율을 통해 국내 경기에 전달되는 과정을 실제 GDP 통계와 연결해 설명해 주기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It ties the actual GDP figures to price pass-through, menu costs and the way foreign demand reaches Japan's economy through imports and the exchange rate.
